source_excerpts: There are diferent ways of approximating the pricing map (Step (i)): One could consider a pointwise approach where strikes and maturities are input parameters of the pricing map along model parameters. Alternatively to this we also explore the advantages of proceeding here instead with a gridwise approach, by first setting strikes and maturities before learning the map from model parameters to the implied volatility surface (with corresponding strikes and maturities). In this work we showcase a direct comparison these approaches to the learning stage (Step (i)) and present algorithms that provide a suficient accuracy for practical use, but are computationally eficient enough for daily practice on a large scale:

source_excerpts: • The two-step approach also has overwhelming risk management benefits. Firstly, we can understand and interpret the output of our neural network and therefore test the output as a function of model parameters against traditional numerical methods. (Indeed, the output values correspond to option prices in the model under consideration.) The second overwhelming advantage is that existing risk management libraries of models remain valid with minimal modification. The neural network is only used as a computational enhancement of models, and therefore, the knowledge and intuition gathered in many years of experience with traditional models remains useful.
